target.queryText:
-- bms_state_charge, not charge_state: 0x201 byte 0 is a bitfield, so charging
-- while balancing reads 0x06 and a `charge_state = 2` test would miss it entirely.
-- The decoder already publishes the bit (registry.ts), so the mask lives in one place.
WITH samples AS (
  SELECT r.ts, r.value, LAG(r.value) OVER (ORDER BY r.ts) AS previous_value
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key = 'bms_state_charge'
),
sessions AS (
  SELECT ts,
    -- no later clearing sample means the session is still running: run the band
    -- to the right edge of the window rather than collapsing it to zero width.
    -- An unterminated session is indistinguishable from a running one here, so a
    -- session whose clearing sample was never recorded (service killed mid-charge,
    -- bike unplugged while the BMS was asleep) paints to the right edge of every
    -- window from then on. That is the right default; it is also where to look first
    -- if a charge band looks implausibly long.
    COALESCE((SELECT MIN(later.ts) FROM samples later WHERE later.ts > samples.ts AND later.value <> 1),
             $__to) AS ended
  FROM samples
  WHERE value = 1 AND (previous_value IS NULL OR previous_value <> 1)
)
SELECT ts/1000.0 AS time, ended/1000.0 AS timeEnd,
  'Charge session (0x201 state bit 1)' AS text,
  'bms_state_charge' AS tags
FROM sessions
-- overlap, not containment, so a session that began before the window still draws
WHERE ts <= $__to AND ended >= $__from
ORDER BY ts

description: Isolation test, BMS error and warning flags, and diagnostic code counts, decoded from CAN signals and the Connectivity Hub. Every series is logged on change with a per-signal deadband, so flat stretches are held values rather than missing telemetry. The deadband is 0 for the error and warning bits but 10 counts for iso_test_1/2/total, so a flat isolation trace means “no move larger than 10 counts” rather than “no move”.

panels.description: Latest |512 − IsoTest1|, in 10-bit ADC counts. 512 is the ideal; the deviation is the leak magnitude and a real leak moves tens of counts. IsoTest1 high means the leak sits nearer the positive terminal. The first colour step is 12 rather than 10 because the signal carries deadband 10 (registry.ts): within one service run nothing under an 11-count move is ever stored, so a smaller number on this tile is a stale reading, not a measured deviation. Red past 60. The reading only means anything above 25 VDC, so it is meaningless with the pack contactors open.

targets.queryText:
SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, ABS(512 - r.value) AS value
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
-- no lower bound: log-on-change means the last change can predate the window,
-- and a held value is the honest answer where "No data" reads as a dead logger.
WHERE s.key = 'iso_test_1' AND r.ts <= $__to
ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Leak detected (error bit 16)

panels.description: IsoTest1 and IsoTest2 in raw 10-bit ADC counts, with a flat reference series at the ideal of 512. The axis is soft-clamped to 500-524, which is one deadband either side of the ideal — the smallest move these signals can record (deadband 10, registry.ts) is therefore roughly the full height of the clamped axis, and it expands on its own if a real leak moves further. Step interpolation with spanNulls: a flat stretch means no move larger than 10 counts rather than data going missing — a weaker statement than log-on-change makes elsewhere on this dashboard, and the two signals are written milliseconds apart so widening them into one table leaves nulls that have to be spanned.

targets.queryText:
-- Seeded at both ends. iso_test_* carries deadband 10 and lastLogged resets on restart,
-- so in practice these only log once per service boot: a window containing no restart
-- returns nothing at all, and the panel reads "No data" for a signal whose held value is
-- perfectly well defined.
-- Two seed rows per series, not one. Grafana pins the x scale to the dashboard time
-- range, so a lone sample from before $__from is clipped out of the plot area; and
-- stepAfter draws segments between consecutive points rather than extending past the
-- last one, so a single off-screen point draws no line at all. The second row restamps
-- the last known value at $__to, which gives the step two points to span and is exactly
-- what carry-forward means. ORDER BY time over the whole union keeps the plugin's
-- global-ascending-time rule.
SELECT time, metric, value FROM (
  SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, s.key AS metric, r.value AS value
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key IN ('iso_test_1', 'iso_test_2') AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts/1000.0, s.key, r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'iso_test_1' AND r.ts < $__from ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts/1000.0, s.key, r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'iso_test_2' AND r.ts < $__from ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT $__to/1000.0, s.key, r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'iso_test_1' AND r.ts <= $__to ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT $__to/1000.0, s.key, r.value
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'iso_test_2' AND r.ts <= $__to ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
)
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Deviation from ideal — |512 − count|

panels.description: The BMS flags an isolation leak when IsoTestTotal rises above the measured pack voltage, so the two are plotted on one axis and compared directly — the gap between the lines is the margin. Counts and volts share an axis here because the comparison itself is unit-free. IsoTestTotal steps (deadband 10, so it holds between samples); pack voltage is drawn with linear interpolation because it is a densely sampled analogue value that really does move between samples — but it keeps the panel's default of showing points, because it is also seeded to the window edges and a linear segment from a seed sample would otherwise be an unmarked ramp through values that were never measured. Where the points are far apart, the line between them is drawn, not read. spanNulls on both, since widening two signals with different timestamps into one table inserts nulls that are not gaps in the data.

-- while CAN is streaming: a parked bike with the BMS asleep produces no rows at all, and
-- that is precisely the state in which iso_test_total needs its own seed. Unseeded, panel
-- 8 would show a held IsoTestTotal against a missing threshold, which is the half of the
-- comparison that carries the meaning. Longest pack_v gap in the 2026-08-02 file: 26 min.
-- Two seed rows per series, not one. Grafana pins the x scale to the dashboard time
-- range, so a lone sample from before $__from is clipped out of the plot area; and
-- stepAfter draws segments between consecutive points rather than extending past the

-- the last known value at $__to, which gives the step two points to span and is exactly

panels.title: IsoTestTotal vs pack voltage (the leak threshold)

panels.description: The eight decoded booleans out of the BMS error and warning words. A state timeline rather than a line chart: these are two-valued, and what matters is which stretch of time a bit was set, not the shape of a line between 0 and 1. Each bar holds its state until the next sample, which is how log-on-change data is meant to be read — a long unbroken bar is a flag that stayed put, not a signal that stopped reporting. The query turns each flag into the words 'clear' and 'ACTIVE' and groups on whole seconds, so the eight flags out of one 0x201 decode land on the same row instead of eight rows that are mostly empty. 'error: over temperature' merges error bits 4 and 7 (cell and LMU) and 'error: contactor' merges bits 21-25, matching the decoder.

targets.queryText:
-- MIN(), not MAX(): SQLite compares text with BINARY collation, so 'ACTIVE' < 'clear'
-- and MIN is severity-first. A flag that both sets and clears inside one second-bucket
-- must render ACTIVE, not green. Renaming either state string can silently flip that,
-- so 'ACTIVE' has to keep sorting before the cleared label.
SELECT r.ts/1000 AS time,
  MIN(CASE WHEN s.key = 'bms_err_cell_overvoltage'    THEN state END) AS "error: cell overvoltage",
  MIN(CASE WHEN s.key = 'bms_err_cell_undervoltage'   THEN state END) AS "error: cell undervoltage",
  MIN(CASE WHEN s.key = 'bms_err_over_temp'           THEN state END) AS "error: over temperature",
  MIN(CASE WHEN s.key = 'bms_err_leak_detected'       THEN state END) AS "error: leak detected",
  MIN(CASE WHEN s.key = 'bms_err_leak_detect_failed'  THEN state END) AS "error: leak detect failed",
  MIN(CASE WHEN s.key = 'bms_err_contactor'           THEN state END) AS "error: contactor",
  MIN(CASE WHEN s.key = 'bms_warn_low_soc'            THEN state END) AS "warning: low SOC",
  MIN(CASE WHEN s.key = 'bms_warn_balancing_required' THEN state END) AS "warning: balancing required"
FROM (
  SELECT r.ts, r.signal_id, CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'ACTIVE' ELSE 'clear' END AS state
  FROM reading r
  WHERE r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
  -- Seeded from before $__from only. A state-timeline region runs until the next sample or
  -- the end of the time range, so the last state already extends to the right edge on its
  -- own   -- unlike a timeseries, this needs no $__to row. Without the left seed a quiet
  -- window returns nothing and the panel blanks, which is the failure the stat tiles were
  -- fixed for.
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts, r.signal_id, CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'ACTIVE' ELSE 'clear' END
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal seed ON seed.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE seed.key = 'bms_err_cell_overvoltage' AND r.ts < $__from ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts, r.signal_id, CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'ACTIVE' ELSE 'clear' END
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal seed ON seed.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE seed.key = 'bms_err_cell_undervoltage' AND r.ts < $__from ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts, r.signal_id, CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'ACTIVE' ELSE 'clear' END
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal seed ON seed.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE seed.key = 'bms_err_over_temp' AND r.ts < $__from ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts, r.signal_id, CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'ACTIVE' ELSE 'clear' END
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal seed ON seed.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE seed.key = 'bms_err_leak_detected' AND r.ts < $__from ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts, r.signal_id, CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'ACTIVE' ELSE 'clear' END
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal seed ON seed.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE seed.key = 'bms_err_leak_detect_failed' AND r.ts < $__from ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts, r.signal_id, CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'ACTIVE' ELSE 'clear' END
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal seed ON seed.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE seed.key = 'bms_err_contactor' AND r.ts < $__from ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts, r.signal_id, CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'ACTIVE' ELSE 'clear' END
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal seed ON seed.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE seed.key = 'bms_warn_low_soc' AND r.ts < $__from ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts, r.signal_id, CASE WHEN r.value <> 0 THEN 'ACTIVE' ELSE 'clear' END
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal seed ON seed.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE seed.key = 'bms_warn_balancing_required' AND r.ts < $__from ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
) AS r
JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
-- the bare ts predicate inside the derived table is not a scan: SQLite flattens the
-- subquery and pushes this key filter down, so the plan is
-- SEARCH r USING INDEX idx_reading_sig_ts (signal_id=? AND ts>? AND ts<?).
WHERE s.key IN ('bms_err_cell_overvoltage', 'bms_err_cell_undervoltage', 'bms_err_over_temp',
                'bms_err_leak_detected', 'bms_err_leak_detect_failed', 'bms_err_contactor',
                'bms_warn_low_soc', 'bms_warn_balancing_required')
GROUP BY r.ts/1000
ORDER BY time

panels.title: LMU comm warnings

panels.description: The code count in mode 01 PID 01, byte A bits 0-6, polled over OBD-II. This is STORED history and it only climbs: 37 in late July, 38 on 2026-08-02, 39 on 2026-08-04. It is not the number of faults active right now — dtc_list_count next to it is, and the two disagree for that reason rather than because either is wrong.

targets.queryText:
SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time, r.value AS value
FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
-- no lower bound: log-on-change means the last change can predate the window,
-- and a held value is the honest answer where "No data" reads as a dead logger.
WHERE s.key = 'dtc_count' AND r.ts <= $__to
ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: dtc_count — OBD PID 01

panels.description: The number of codes in the list the Connectivity Hub returns (message type 25). Settled 2026-08-04: this is the CURRENTLY ACTIVE list, while dtc_count next to it is stored history. It flickered between 1 and 0 across 11 of 47 once-a-minute polls in one 47-minute capture, riding and DC charging alike, while PID 01 held at 39 — stored history cannot flicker. The one code seen so far is P0A07, the open coolant-pump driver. Expect 0 here most of the time; a 0 is not proof the bike is fault-free between polls.

panels.title: MIL lamp (mil_on)

panels.description: dtc_count and dtc_list_count over time, deliberately drawn as two separate series rather than reconciled into one number. They come from different transports — OBD-II mode 01 PID 01 against the Connectivity Hub's own code list — and they count different things: dtc_count is stored history, which only climbs (39 as of 2026-08-04), and dtc_list_count is the currently active list, which flaps between 1 and 0 as the pump-driver fault comes and goes. Neither is the fault count on its own, which is why both are drawn. Step interpolation with spanNulls: both are logged on change and at unrelated timestamps, so each line holds until its own next sample and the nulls that widening introduces are not missing data.

panels.description: The bms_io_state byte from frame 0x206 split into its eight bits, where bit n is IO n+1. A state timeline because each bit is a two-valued line whose interesting property is how long it stayed high. Worth watching next to the isolation panels: in the current file the byte goes 0x13 to 0x87 and back over the same stretch that the BMS reports charging, which is the same stretch where IsoTest2 moves off 511. What each IO line is wired to is not established. All eight bits come out of one byte, so each sample fills every row and each bar holds its state until bms_io_state is logged again — flat is a held value, not a dropout.

targets.queryText:
-- Seeded from before $__from only. A state-timeline region runs until the next sample or
-- the end of the time range, so the last state already extends to the right edge on its
-- own -- unlike a timeseries, this needs no $__to row. Without the left seed a quiet
-- window returns nothing and the panel blanks, which is the failure the stat tiles were
-- fixed for.
SELECT time, "IO1", "IO2", "IO3", "IO4", "IO5", "IO6", "IO7", "IO8" FROM (
  SELECT r.ts/1000.0 AS time,
  CASE WHEN (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 0) & 1 = 1 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END AS "IO1",
  CASE WHEN (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 1) & 1 = 1 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END AS "IO2",
  CASE WHEN (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 2) & 1 = 1 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END AS "IO3",
  CASE WHEN (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 3) & 1 = 1 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END AS "IO4",
  CASE WHEN (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 4) & 1 = 1 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END AS "IO5",
  CASE WHEN (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 5) & 1 = 1 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END AS "IO6",
  CASE WHEN (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 6) & 1 = 1 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END AS "IO7",
  CASE WHEN (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 7) & 1 = 1 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END AS "IO8"
  FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
  WHERE s.key = 'bms_io_state' AND r.ts BETWEEN $__from AND $__to
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (SELECT r.ts/1000.0,
                        CASE WHEN (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 0) & 1 = 1 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END,
                        CASE WHEN (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 1) & 1 = 1 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END,
                        CASE WHEN (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 2) & 1 = 1 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END,
                        CASE WHEN (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 3) & 1 = 1 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END,
                        CASE WHEN (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 4) & 1 = 1 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END,
                        CASE WHEN (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 5) & 1 = 1 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END,
                        CASE WHEN (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 6) & 1 = 1 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END,
                        CASE WHEN (CAST(r.value AS INTEGER) >> 7) & 1 = 1 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END
                 FROM reading r JOIN signal s ON s.id = r.signal_id
                 WHERE s.key = 'bms_io_state' AND r.ts < $__from ORDER BY r.ts DESC LIMIT 1)
)
ORDER BY time
